takeaway: IMN Friday keeps Pacífico Norte in rainy-season mode: morning partly cloudy, afternoon scattered showers with storms, and possible coastal rains at night (Nicoya ~35°C; Liberia ~36.5°C). Surf-wind regime remains Pacific/monsoon onshore–side (SW–W 850), not Caribbean trades — expect choppier faces vs classic easterly glass. Hurricane Polo is a Category 5 well offshore southwestern Mexico (~17.2°N/107.5°W); Odalys stays far west; Tehuantepec genesis is high (~90% in 7 days) tracking parallel to southern/southwestern Mexico — no cyclone near Costa Rica. Gyre/temporales watch stays elevated, not established: ensemble means keep Pacific SW low-level moisture into Nicoya through the weekend into early next week, without a closed land gyre. IMN weekly flags Tropical Wave #47 Sat–Sun as a possible afternoon-rain boost.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun)
periods.pattern: Today (IMN Pacífico Norte, valid Fri 25 Sep): morning partly cloudy; afternoon partly cloudy to cloudy with scattered showers and storms; evening partly cloudy with possible coastal rains. Nicoya max ~35.0°C / min ~23.8°C (Liberia ~36.5°C). General commentary: weak winds, sea breezes, and humidity favoring afternoon storms on the Pacific slope, Valle Central, and central Zona Norte; maritime Pacific instability this morning; probable localized coastal Pacific showers early night. Weekly: typical rainy-season pattern; Tropical Wave #47 this weekend (especially Sat–Sun) may increase afternoon instability/rain. GFS 06Z / GEFS mean 06Z / EPS mean 00Z / AIFS-ENS 00Z 24-h maps keep Nicoya mostly light–moderate (~0.1–0.5 in / 24 h Fri–Sat window; GEFS f024 ~0.1–0.4 in). GEFS mean epac f024 and EPS/AIFS f024 show light SW–W 850 onshore over Nicoya with flanking EPAC lows (GEFS ~1010 hPa class near Guatemala/El Salvador waters; EPS det-type deep TC lows ~979–988 hPa well west near Mexico) — moist monsoon trough / ITCZ, not a closed land gyre. Papagayo: Fri afternoon NW–N ~10 kt; Fri night Papagayo briefly E 10–15 kt then S–SW; seas ~4–6 ft (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113).
periods.implications: Mornings still the better outdoor window; plan around afternoon scattered storms (IMN Pac Norte) and possible coastal night rains. Inland Guanacaste stays very hot. Surf: Pacific onshore–side regime — prefer overnight/early-morning lulls; do not expect all-day trade glass. Watch Sat–Sun if OT#47 verifies wetter.
periods.confidence: High for no nearby TC and continued ITCZ shower/storm chances (IMN + NHC). Moderate on exact Nosara timing/amounts (IMN scattered storms vs light–moderate ensemble means; OT#47 weekend boost uncertain).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon–Thu)
periods.pattern: IMN weekly anticipates a slight decrease in Pacific rains early next week, though isolated afternoon showers/storms can still occur. Mon (~28 Sep): GEFS mean 06Z epac f072 keeps W–SSW 850 over Nicoya with ~1006 hPa EPAC L south of Mexico and deeper TC-type lows farther west; EPS mean 00Z f072 shows ~1004 hPa L south of southern Mexico with light SW 850 over Nicoya; AIFS-ENS 00Z f072 similar (~1004 hPa L, W–SW 850) and wetter over Nicoya (~0.5–1.0 in / 24 h) than EPS (~0.2–0.5 in) or GEFS (~0.1–0.4 in). GFS deterministic 06Z epac f072 deepens a Mexico-parallel TC (~968 hPa class west of mainland) plus a ~999 hPa L south of Mexico — treat deep features as Mexico-parallel TC environment (Polo / Tehuantepec genesis), not a Costa Rica gyre. By ~Wed 30 (f120), GEFS mean still shows S–SSW 850 over Nicoya with precip ~0.5–0.75 in; EPS f120 also light SW/SSW 850 without a closed land gyre. NHC OFFPZ8: moderate-or-weaker winds into early next week; Papagayo Sun–Mon often variable <5 kt with seas ~4–6 ft. Not locked as a multi-day temporal or closed Central American gyre.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible Mon–Wed if SW moisture holds; treat deeper EPS/AIFS/GFS EPAC lows as Mexico-parallel moisture signal, not a guaranteed temporales. Marine: Papagayo mostly light/S or variable with seas ~4–6 ft (NHC). Surf regime stays Pacific onshore–side on ensemble means through midweek.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances and persistent SW-moisture signal; low–moderate for sustained temporales or a closed Central American gyre (ensemble means lack a closed land gyre; Nicoya precip stays mostly light–moderate except AIFS wetter outlier).

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (28 Sep–25 Oct) keeps Pacífico Norte dry/below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm for 28 Sep–4 Oct, then 1–70 mm 5–11 Oct) with stronger Pacific deficit into mid–late October; no extreme-event call for 28 Sep–4 Oct. CPC GTH text updated 22 Sep (valid 30 Sep–13 Oct): very strong El Niño background; week-2/3 EPAC genesis areas lean Mexico / open EPAC, not CR; discussion notes El Niño shear over Mexico/Caribbean may ease later as MJO evolves — not a CR-focused extreme rainfall call. GEFS mean f168 (~2 Oct) still shows light–moderate precip over Nicoya (~0.5–0.75 in / 24 h) without a local extreme bullseye or closed land gyre. Heavy EPAC precip stays offshore Mexico. Single deterministic frames can still show a wetter day — treat as scenario only.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible. Official sub-seasonal leans drier than a temporales regime.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly weekend into early next week (~Sat–Tue 26–29 Sep) while flanking EPAC lows, Pacific SW low-level flow, and IMN OT#47 weekend timing overlap; GEFS mean still keeps Nicoya onshore SW/SSW through f120 rather than a clean trade return
gyreWatch.supporting: GEFS mean 06Z f024–f120 shows SW–W/SSW 850 over Nicoya (epac panels clearest) with EPAC Ls ~1006–1010 hPa class; EPS mean 00Z f024–f072 and AIFS-ENS 00Z f072 keep SW onshore fetch and broader EPAC lows (~1004 hPa class south of Mexico). Short-term IMN ITCZ / Pac Norte afternoon storms + possible coastal night rains + weekly OT#47 Sat–Sun support a moist Pacific weekend. Tehuantepec genesis now ~90% in 7 days (up from ~80% Thu) adds Mexico-parallel moisture risk. Versus Thursday, SW-moisture window still extends through early next week on ensemble means; AIFS f072 is wetter over Nicoya than EPS/GEFS.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Ensemble means do not show a closed gyre centered over Central America — pattern is flanking EPAC lows / monsoon trough plus SW moisture. GFS det deep EPAC lows are TC-type features near Mexico (Polo / next Tehuantepec system), not a CR gyre. Ensemble-mean Nicoya precip stays mostly light–moderate (EPS/GEFS); only AIFS is wetter locally. NHC has no disturbance near Costa Rica (Cat-5 Polo and Hurricane Odalys well west/NW; Tehuantepec genesis tracks parallel to southern/southwestern Mexico). IMN sub-seasonal still favors Pacific rainfall deficit from 28 Sep onward. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities.

surfWinds.detail: GEFS/EPS/AIFS keep light SW–W to SSW 850 over Nicoya through the weekend into early next week with flanking EPAC lows — Pacific-side moisture/monsoon trough, not E–NE Caribbean trades. Nicaragua proxy: maps do NOT show all-day Nica offshore trades; Pacific SW flow dominates the isthmus low levels, so do not expect Nosara all-day offshore glass. NHC OFFPZ8 Papagayo is mostly light/S or variable with seas ~4–6 ft; a brief Fri-night Papagayo E 10–15 kt pulse is marine surface only and is not the same as glassy Caribbean-trade offshore at Nosara's west-facing beaches.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Fri–Sun: no clean all-day trade-offshore signal. Prefer the lightest overnight–early morning lulls before afternoon convection; expect generally choppier Pacific/onshore-side flow vs classic easterly glass. Brief Fri-night easterly Papagayo (OFFPZ8) may help overnight glass locally, then daytime S/SW returns. Watch for any GEFS flip back toward E–NE trades (not showing through ~f120 in this morning’s means).
surfWinds.confidence: High that the large-scale regime is Pacific SW rather than trades for days 1–7; moderate on exact beach-face chop vs lull timing (850 used as regime proxy; marine surface is light/variable with a short overnight easterly pulse).

Weekly now highlights Tropical Wave #47 this weekend Sat–Sun (yesterday referenced OT#46). Sub-seasonal rolled forward to 28 Sep–25 Oct and still keeps Pac Norte dry/deficit. Thu evening IMN aviso (5:30 p.m.) emphasized Nicoya peninsula for late-day/early-night storms with 15–40 mm / 6 h (local max ~80 mm) — no new Friday aviso listed yet at collection time. Polo regained Category 5 (~160 mph / 929 mb near 17.2°N/107.5°W at 0900 UTC Fri), farther west offshore SW Mexico; Odalys remains a hurricane well west; Tehuantepec genesis raised to ~90% in 7 days (was ~80%). NHC OFFPZ8: Papagayo Fri afternoon NW–N 10 kt, Fri night brief E 10–15 then S/SW weekend, seas ~4–6 ft (yesterday often 3–6 ft). Model theme similar to Thu: SW moisture persists into f120, with AIFS f072 wetter over Nicoya than EPS/GEFS — still no closed land gyre.
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Fri–Sun before the convective peak, noting IMN afternoon scattered storms on Pac Norte and a possible OT#47 weekend bump Sat–Sun. Worth planning around: possible coastal night rains, very warm inland heat (Liberia ~36.5°C; Nicoya ~35°C), and Papagayo light/S or variable with seas ~4–6 ft (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113). Surf: Pacific onshore–side regime — chase overnight/early-morning lulls, not all-day glass. Watch Sat–Tue if SW moisture / OT#47 / Tehuantepec moisture verify wetter than GEFS.
